claim: I-SME gives the same final mapping as batch SME when all facts arrive at once, at no extra asymptotic cost.
agent_test: Run extend-per-round vs re-map-from-scratch on the same facts; compare final mapping and tokens.

claim: I-SME keeps at most n global mappings within p% of best, and reports the fraction of possible structure matched, so a controller can decide when to remap.
agent_test: Keep a small set of rival mappings with scores; trigger re-map when the coverage fraction stalls. Gap search: no successor numbers found.

claim: Delivering facts in an unhelpful order doubles human solve time (178.0 s vs 363.1 s) and doubles I-SME remaps (1.5 vs 3.0).
agent_test: Order the same case facts easy-first vs hard-first; count mapping revisions and tokens to a correct answer. Human numbers are second-hand (Keane in press, unopened); model fit is two example sets, no stats. Gap search: gap search found no replication (tool-limited).

claim: Time-limited comparison of scenes shows early matches by feature/object similarity, with relational alignment arriving later; models of this use incremental mapping.
agent_test: Compare answer quality under a short vs long thinking budget on cross-mapped items; expect surface errors at short budgets.
audit_note: The two Lovett et al. papers (2006 proceedings and 2009 journal) are one research group, and Goldstone and Medin / Sloutsky and Yarlas data are only read second-hand through them; incremental-mapping models are all this one group's.

claim: An incremental, serial mapping model can solve 56/60 Raven Standard Progressive Matrices (75th percentile) from symbolic-visual input.
agent_test: Not directly testable on text; use as proof that mapping-by-extension scales to matrix tasks.

claim: Progressive alignment (easy same-dimension comparisons first) helps a model learn relational similarity; the model hit 100% on same-dimension triads while children were at 68%.
agent_test: Present analogous cases in a curriculum from close to far in the prompt; compare with random order at equal tokens. Kotovsky and Gentner details second-hand. Gap search: d09 is a model of the child result only; no LLM test found.

claim: Pragmatic filters are needed in practice: without an identical-functions filter, MARS matched specific enthalpy to temperature and produced a wrong answer.
agent_test: Ablate a type or role check in the mapper and count wrong cross-quantity matches.

claim: Candidate inferences must be checked jointly for consistency, not one by one.
agent_test: Batch-check all transferred inferences for joint consistency; compare to per-inference checks. Gap search: no joint-vs-per-inference LLM test found.

claim: One-shot LLM analogy results depend on familiar formats: GPT-3 beat humans on digit matrices (OR 1.88; MC OR 6.27) and letter strings (OR 1.76, p=6.3e-5 overall), but humans were better on story analogies (OR 0.37).
agent_test: Baseline only.

claim: On counterfactual (altered alphabet / permuted) tasks LLM accuracy falls (humans 0.753; GPT-4 0.488 on letter strings) while humans stay flat; the gap is partly contested because many GPT errors use a valid alternative rule (46% vs 39% of human errors).
agent_test: Test the agent on altered-rule variants; score alternative-valid answers separately.

claim: Story-analogy answers shift with option order and paraphrase for GPT-4 (0.89 first vs 0.61 second; 0.86 vs 0.72 paraphrased) while humans do not (0.78 both).
agent_test: Shuffle option and fact order in S6 prompts; require stable answers across two orders.

claim: In letter-string analogies (Stevenson et al.), GPT-4o accuracy fell from 0.85 with the Latin alphabet to 0.63 with Greek and 0.48 with symbols, while adults stayed at 0.88-0.91; other work finds LLMs match humans in several analogy conditions, so transfer failure is task-dependent.
agent_test: Run S6 on unfamiliar tokens to test whether mapping is structural or lexical.
audit_note: Stevenson et al. numbers verified (GPT-4o 0.85/0.63/0.48; adults 0.88/0.91/0.89), but Webb et al. show GPT-3 generalizing letter strings to concepts and Musker et al. report LLMs matching humans in several conditions, so a general failure to transfer is not supported.
claim_before_audit: LLM analogy skill does not transfer well across symbol sets: GPT-4o 0.85 Latin, 0.63 Greek, 0.48 Symbol versus adults 0.88-0.91.

claim: Self-generated analogs and exemplars give small gains on reasoning (GSM8K 11% to 13-15% for GPT-3.5) and are scale-dependent.
agent_test: Compare self-generated vs retrieved exemplars at equal tokens. Table cells were garbled; treat as approximate.

claim: No study found tests incremental analogical mapping in an LLM directly; all analogy LLM work is one-shot.
agent_test: This is the open slot the agent can fill: extend-vs-redo mapping across rounds. Gap search: gap search again found no direct test.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Facts arriving over several turns hurt LLMs: average 39% drop in multi-turn sharded vs full instruction; aptitude -16% (not significant), unreliability +112%; all-at-once CONCAT keeps 95.1%.
agent_test: Feed the same facts in one block vs in rounds; measure accuracy and variance at equal tokens. (Verified in paper text.) Gap search: d06: sequential presentation of hypotheses costs accuracy in 14-16 of 17 models.

claim: Restating all facts at the end (RECAP) or snowballing history recovers only 15-20% of multi-turn loss.
agent_test: Add a consolidation restatement step before S6 extension; compare with plain history.

claim: Premise order changes accuracy: drops of 20-30% for GPT-4-turbo/PaLM 2-L, over 40 points for weaker models.
agent_test: Present facts in two orders and require agreement before committing.

claim: Prompt order sensitivity is large and not transferable across model sizes (SST-2 near 50% to over 85%; permutation scores across 175B and 2.7B correlate 0.05).
agent_test: Randomise fact order per sample and measure variance; do not tune order on a small model.
audit_note: Lu et al. verified (permutations 88.7 vs 51.6 percent on SST-2; 175B vs 2.7B correlation 0.05); Chen et al. concerns premise order, not model-size transfer.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction does not reliably help: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8 and GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 over repeated rounds; oracle labels help (GSM8K 84.3 / 97.5).
agent_test: Allow revision only with an external check; compare against no-revision at equal tokens.

claim: Models flip correct answers under pushback (first-answer change 32% GPT-4 to 86% Claude 1.3; accuracy drops up to 27%), so new facts may overwrite a good mapping wrongly.
agent_test: Insert a neutral new fact that should not change the answer; count flips. Gap search: flips compound over rounds (d05: up to 47% accuracy drop) and 43.5% of flips went toward correct (d08); gate on evidence, not on change.
audit_note: Accuracy drop of 27% is an average over six datasets (Claude 1.3); final clause is an inference, hedged with 'may'.

claim: Belief revision is weak: best large models reach at most 50% on BREU (update plus maintain); plan-and-solve adds about 1%.
agent_test: Test update-vs-maintain accuracy when a new fact should or should not change the mapping. Gap search: AGM-Bench: models keep retracted facts and drop unrelated ones; BayesBench: larger models over-update.

claim: Models learn from rounds poorly without help: original LLMs plateau after round 1 in a 5-round preference task, while Bayesian-teaching-tuned ones keep improving.
agent_test: Keep an explicit running belief state across rounds and compare to history only.

claim: Grounded feedback loops help: Reflexion solved 130/134 ALFWorld tasks; Voyager lost 73% of items without self-verification; Self-Refine +8.7 points on code, most gain early.
agent_test: Grounded check after each extension; stop after 2-3 rounds.
audit_note: Numbers match; 'grounded' label is loose since Self-Refine uses model-generated feedback, and Voyager's self-verification is also LLM-based.

claim: Models lose over 20% accuracy when the answer sits in the middle of a long context (Liu et al., GPT-3.5 multi-document QA), and Cumulative Reasoning, which accumulates verified propositions, improves FOLIO-wiki accuracy by up to 8.62 points over direct prompting and about 4.3 points over CoT (GPT-3.5-turbo); this suggests but does not show that an explicit proposition store beats long free-text context.
agent_test: Store mapping and facts as a compact structure; re-read the structure each round.
audit_note: 8.62 is the gain of CR (GPT-3.5, FOLIO-wiki) over Direct prompting (CoT gain is +4.31, so over CoT it is about 4.3); neither paper tests an explicit structured store versus free-text context (lost-in-the-middle only compares input positions).
claim_before_audit: Keeping facts in an explicit structured store beats long free-text context: lost-in-the-middle drops of over 20%, and cumulative reasoning with a stored proposition set gains up to 8.62% over CoT.

claim: Mechanistically, in-context analogy uses concept vectors, and the first pair carries the rule; patching it fixes up to 38.4% of errors.
agent_test: Put the clearest example pair first and restate the rule explicitly.
audit_note: Opielka et al. is about antonym-type concept vectors from ICL heads, not analogy per se; 38.4% is a best case (Gemma-7B) of incorrect cases fixed by replacing the first pair.

claim: Hybrid structure-mapper plus LLM abstraction beats LLM-only on small models (Llama-3.1-8B 0.45 vs 0.28 on story MCQ) but not uniformly (Qwen far ARN 0.47 vs 0.52).
agent_test: Explicit slot-alignment table plus LLM abstraction vs LLM alone; 2026 preprint, treat cautiously. Gap search: d11: FAME is a second SME-plus-LLM hybrid, not yet tested here.

claim: In multi-turn use, a challenge that arrives after the model has answered flips correct answers more than the same claim in the first query (6.99% vs 2.53%, 2.8x), but fake sources lower flipping in multi-turn while raising it in single-turn.
agent_test: Run the same new fact as an opening premise vs a later correction and count flipped slots.

claim: Presenting competing hypotheses one at a time costs accuracy against showing them together (14/17 to 16/17 models below single-shot; up to 30% average tax), and the same holds for rebuttals judged in sequence vs side by side.
agent_test: On a new fact, show old mapping and new alternative side by side in one comparison step.
audit_note: Guo et al. counts are per benchmark (14/17 MedQA, 14/17 JAMA CC, 16/17 MedMCQA); 'up to 30%' is a maximum average.

claim: LLM belief revision shows both inertia (retracted facts kept) and collateral damage (unrelated beliefs dropped); there is a trade-off: systems that follow updates well resist drift poorly, and RAG helps update tracking (+0.09 BRA) but not drift resistance (+0.02 DCS).
agent_test: After a conflicting fact, re-derive affected slots only and re-check unrelated slots for unchanged status.
audit_note: BeliefShift's trade-off is about personalising vs fact-grounded models; AGM-Bench does not frame a trade-off itself, only inertia and collateral damage.

claim: Larger LLMs track a hidden quantity better across turns but over-react to evidence, giving more extreme probabilities than the Bayesian reference.
agent_test: Keep per-slot scores with a bounded step per round.

claim: No replication of Keane's order effect and no accuracy or speed numbers for I-SME successors (Bridge, Companion sessions) were found; the order effect remains one 1994 result. Searches were tool-limited, so this is not proof of absence.
agent_test: Run the order experiment on the agent itself before relying on K03.
